family_A_active_interrogation.concept: Controlled perturbation of valve → transient response → hydraulic parameter estimation
family_A_active_interrogation.independent_claim: A method of interrogating an endovascular CSF-to-venous shunt system, comprising: (a) deploying a shunt having a valve between a subarachnoid space and a dural venous sinus; (b) controlling said valve to transition between an open state and a closed state; (c) measuring at least CSF pressure and venous pressure during said transition; (d) estimating at least one hydraulic parameter of said shunt from the measured pressure response; (e) comparing said estimated parameter to an expected parameter; and (f) classifying a failure state of said shunt based on said comparison.
family_A_active_interrogation.design_around_risk: MEDIUM — competitor could use passive observation instead of active perturbation
family_A_active_interrogation.novelty_basis: No prior art teaches ACTIVE valve perturbation for system identification in a CSF-venous shunt

family_B_state_estimation.concept: Observed pressure/flow/valve relationship → expected transfer function → deviation → state classification
family_B_state_estimation.independent_claim: A method of estimating the hydraulic state of an endovascular CSF shunt, comprising: (a) observing a relationship between CSF pressure, venous pressure, shunt pressure, and valve state over time; (b) computing an observed hydraulic transfer function from said observations; (c) comparing said observed transfer function to an expected transfer function; (d) detecting a deviation indicating a failure mode; and (e) classifying said failure mode from the characteristic signature of said deviation in a multi-variable state space.
family_B_state_estimation.design_around_risk: LOW — covers passive observation + computation, harder to avoid
family_B_state_estimation.novelty_basis: No prior art teaches transfer-function-based state estimation for CSF-venous shunt specifically

family_C_adaptive_interrogation.concept: System chooses next perturbation based on uncertainty (adaptive system identification)
family_C_adaptive_interrogation.independent_claim: A method of adaptively interrogating an endovascular CSF shunt system, comprising: (a) observing a current hydraulic state of said shunt; (b) estimating an uncertainty associated with said current state; (c) if said uncertainty exceeds a threshold, selecting an optimal valve perturbation to maximize information gain; (d) applying said perturbation; (e) observing the response; (f) updating said state estimate; and (g) repeating steps (b)-(f) until said uncertainty falls below said threshold.
family_C_adaptive_interrogation.design_around_risk: LOW — adaptive system identification is a specific method, hard to design around
family_C_adaptive_interrogation.novelty_basis: No prior art teaches ADAPTIVE perturbation selection based on uncertainty for shunt diagnostics
family_C_adaptive_interrogation.ceo_note: C is potentially the most valuable — turns diagnostic algorithm into adaptive system-identification method
